facts.statement: Rimasuchus lived during the Early Miocene.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Miocene

facts.statement: Rimasuchus fossils have been found in Egypt and possibly Libya.
facts.quote: Rimasuchus is an extinct genus of large crocodile from the early Miocene of Egypt and possibly Libya.

facts.statement: The first fossil of Rimasuchus was collected by Lieutenant Colonel Arthur H. Lloyd in Wadi Moghara, Egypt, in the early 20th century.
facts.quote: The first fossil of Rimasuchus an incomplete skull with associated mandible, was collected by lieutenant colonel Arthur H. Lloyd in the early 20th century in Wadi Moghara, Egypt.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen CGM 15597 was described by Fourtau in 1918 as Crocodylus lloydi.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, CGM 15597, was given to the Egyptian Geological Museum and described by Fourtau in 1918 under the name Crocodylus lloydi.

facts.statement: Martin Pickford named the Namibian material Crocodylus gariepensis in 2003, suggesting it was the ancestor of the Nile crocodile.
facts.quote: In 2003 the Namibian material was named Crocodylus gariepensis by Martin Pickford, who suggested that it was the true ancestor of the Nile crocodile.

facts.statement: The name Rimasuchus is derived from the Latin word rima, meaning 'crack', referencing the East African Rift Valley.
facts.quote: The generic name "Rimasuchus" comes from the Latin words rima, meaning "crack", which is referencing the East African rift valley.

facts.statement: The species name lloydi honors Arthur H. Lloyd, the discoverer of the fossils in Egypt.
facts.quote: The species name honors Arthur H. Lloyd, who initially discovered the fossils in Egypt.

facts.statement: Rimasuchus had a short and broad snout, known as brevirostrine.
facts.quote: Rimasuchus has a brevirostrine skull, meaning the snout is short and broad.

facts.statement: Rimasuchus could grow to 7 meters or more in length.
facts.quote: Rimasuchus crecía hasta 7 metros o más de longitud.

facts.statement: Rimasuchus possessed robust and blunt teeth, unlike other crocodiles.
facts.quote: Los dientes de Rimasuchus son robustos y romos, a diferencia de los de otros cocodrilos.

facts.statement: The teeth of Rimasuchus were bicarinated, meaning they had ridges on both the front and back.
facts.quote: Los dientes son bicarinados, los que significa que poseía bordes en el frente y la parte posterior.

facts.statement: Rimasuchus preyed on large mammals, including primitive humans.
facts.quote: Depredaba grandes mamíferos, incluyendo humanos primitivos.

facts.statement: Rimasuchus is now considered more closely related to modern African dwarf crocodiles (Osteolaemus) than to the genus Crocodylus.
facts.quote: It was previously thought to be a species of Crocodylus, but is now thought to be more closely related to the modern African dwarf crocodiles (Osteolaemus).

facts.statement: Rimasuchus is closely related to the modern dwarf crocodile Osteolaemus and belongs to the group Osteolaeminae.
facts.quote: Entre los crocodilinos, Rimasuchus está muy cercanamente relacionado con el actual cocodrilo enano Osteolaemus y se sitúa en el grupo Osteolaeminae.

facts.statement: There has been very little study on ontogenetic variation in Rimasuchus and modern crocodiles.
facts.quote: Ha habido sin embargo muy poco estudio sobre la variación ontogénica en Rimasuchus y los cocodrilos actuales.

facts.statement: It is debated whether some Rimasuchus specimens are actually very large examples of Crocodylus niloticus due to similarities between them.
facts.quote: Hay muchas similitudes entre especímenes de R. lloydi y C. niloticus, y es probable que algunos especímenes de Rimasuchus representen en realidad a ejemplares muy grandes de C. niloticus.

facts.statement: Fossils of Rimasuchus date from approximately 1.88 to 7.44 million years ago.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de estas rocas usualmente datan de 1.88 ± 0.02 to 7.44 ± 0.05 millones de años.

facts.statement: Rimasuchus fossils are found in sandstones and mudstones deposited in lakes and rivers.
facts.quote: Las rocas de Turkana que contienen los fósiles de Rimasuchus son usualmente areniscas o lodolitas poco litificadas que fueron depositadas en lagos y ríos.

facts.statement: The earliest Rimasuchus specimens were found in North Africa, but how the species evolved and spread remains uncertain.
facts.quote: Aunque los ejemplares más tempranos han sido recuperados del norte de África, es aún incierto como evolucionó y se extendió esta especie.

facts.statement: As a large semi-terrestrial predator, Rimasuchus likely competed directly with Nile crocodiles.
facts.quote: Siendo un gran depredador semiterrestre, Rimasuchus probablemente competía directamente con los cocodrilos del Nilo

facts.statement: Rimasuchus bones have been found in situ with other vertebrates including fish, birds, mammals like pigs, elephants, giraffes, bovines, rhinos, primates, and hominids such as Australopithecus afarensis.
facts.quote: Sus huesos han sido hallados in situ con otros vertebrados incluyendo a varias especies de peces y aves, mamíferos tales como cerdos, elefantes, jirafas, bóvidos, rinocerontes, primates e incluso homínidos como Australopithecus afarensis.

facts.statement: Predation by crocodiles, including Rimasuchus, is documented by tooth marks on Homo habilis fossils like OH 7, OH 8, and OH 35 at Olduvai Gorge, Tanzania.
facts.quote: En la Garganta de Olduvai de Tanzania, se ha documentado la depredación a través de marcas de dientes de cocodrilo en los huesos de varios especímenes de homínidos, entre ellos OH 7, OH 8 y OH 35, todos los cuales pertenecen a la especie Homo habilis.

facts.statement: Bone damage on H. habilis remains includes bisected bite marks and perforations characteristic of crocodile predation.
facts.quote: El daño óseo en los restos de H. habilis incluye marcas de mordida biseccionadas y perforaciones, las cuales son propias de la depredación por cocodrilos.

facts.statement: Bone accumulations in beds I and II at the gorge have been specifically attributed to Rimasuchus.
facts.quote: Adicionalmente, las acumulaciones de huesos en los lechos I y II en la garganta han sido atribuidos específicamente a Rimasuchus.

facts.statement: A trench containing primitive bovine bones, horses, specimen OH 7, and stone tools also contained Rimasuchus teeth.
facts.quote: Una zanja que contenía huesos de bovinos primitivos, caballos, el espécimen OH 7 y varias herramientas de piedra también tenía dientes de Rimasuchus.

facts.statement: Rimasuchus belongs to the parent group Osteolaemini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Osteolaemini

facts.statement: Rimasuchus is classified in the family Crocodylidae.
facts.quote: Family: Crocodylidae

facts.statement: Rimasuchus is a member of the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The genus Rimasuchus lived from the Burdigalian to the Late Pleistocene, between 20.45 and 0.0117 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Burdigalian to Late Pleistocene (20.45 to 0.0117 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Rimasuchus was named by Storrs in 2003.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Rimasuchus (genus), Storrs 2003

rejected.statement: Rimasuchus fossils are found in close association with Nile crocodile fossils.
rejected.quote: Sus fósiles se han hallado en cercana asociación con los fósiles del cocodrilo del Nilo.
